findings.title: The reviewed commit fails the formatting gate required by tagged releases
findings.reproduction: At b16c64f, run cargo fmt --check. The retained fix-fmt run returned 1. Without checking out another tree, compare git show b16c64f:src/correct.rs with the same stream formatted by Rust 1.99.1 rustfmt --edition 2024 --emit stdout; diff -u returns 1.
findings.expected: The committed source passes the mandatory formatting gate before CI permits packaging and attestation.
findings.observed: The fold closure and the is_some_and expression need Rustfmt changes. The committed source lacks them. The current working tree contains precisely those formatting corrections and passes cargo fmt --check, but those bytes are not part of b16c64f.
findings.impact: A tag at this commit fails CI and cannot reach the ordinary package job. This is a build failure, not a demonstrated runtime or memory-safety defect.
findings.evidence: AUD-006-evidence/fix-fmt.command.json and fix-fmt.log (local, exit 1); AUD-007-evidence/committed-format-diff.log (local, exit 1, SHA-256 fc21a82f402f738cf2a5403bfb3de58b54f92e924320e0a394bf9f07dc617fb2); current-format.log (local, exit 0).
findings.recommendedFix: Include the existing formatting corrections in a successor commit. Preserve the reviewed commit in history.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo fmt --check must pass on the exact successor commit and the tagged CI workflow must consume that commit.

findings.title: The tagged release pipeline does not enforce the required timing probe
findings.reproduction: Read every run step reachable from release.yml jobs.ci and jobs.package. None builds or runs docs/audits/AUD-006-harnesses/timing, and no step inspects field arithmetic assembly.
findings.expected: A release pipeline described as including the new timing check actually runs that check and stops packaging on failure.
findings.observed: workflow_call and needs: ci correctly enforce existing CI checks. The timing requirement was added only to the manual instructions in AGENTS.md; the callable CI contains formatting, clippy, normal tests and rustdoc.
findings.impact: The automatic release path can attest a future timing regression that passes functional tests. A manual timing preflight can still detect it; this finding does not claim that the current arithmetic fix fails or that no manual check occurs.
findings.evidence: Static review of both complete workflows at the target commit; separate reviewer challenge. The fresh timing run passes, which does not supply an automated future gate.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a required release job that builds the timing harness with --locked --release, runs its timing binary, and gates package on its success. State the fields and compiler configurations covered.
findings.requiredVerification: Review the job dependency graph; demonstrate that a deliberately failing timing check prevents package/attest. Cover multiplication and inversion separately where the guarantee requires them.

findings.title: Several new oracle probes report mismatches without failing the command
findings.reproduction: Trace the mismatch counters to each main function exit. fields prints disagreements/bad_products/bad_inverses/bad_slow and boundary errors without checking them; decode prints and then shadows its tallies; cyclic prints total.bad and returns. Most apply_cross observations are only printed. The two unexpected non-Changes repair-plan branches in mhfe print NOT REPAIRED without calling fail().
findings.expected: As the harness README promises, any oracle disagreement makes the relevant command exit nonzero.
findings.observed: These mismatch paths reach a successful return unless a separate assertion happens to fail. Other mhfe mismatch paths already call fail()/finish(); this finding is limited to the unchecked paths.
findings.impact: An automated rerun that checks only exit status can accept incorrect arithmetic, decoding or plan binding. Reviewing printed counters remains possible. No actual production oracle disagreement was demonstrated in this audit.
findings.evidence: Complete source review of the new probes and an independent challenge. This is source-level control-flow evidence; no modified production implementation was executed to simulate a mismatch.
findings.recommendedFix: Accumulate all mismatch counters and fail once at the end, or assert each required result and unchanged-output condition. Treat equivalent-code positive controls separately from negative cases.
findings.requiredVerification: Give each probe a deterministic negative control that produces a mismatch and must exit nonzero, then rerun the unchanged positive oracle cases.

findings.title: The dependency notice incorrectly attributes LoongArch64 libc to cpufeatures
findings.expected: The notice describes dependencies reachable through the pinned sha2 version for each named target.
findings.observed: The notice adds LoongArch64 Linux to libc through cpufeatures. sha2 0.11.1 selects cpufeatures only on AArch64, x86 and x86-64. The LoongArch64 tree without protect contains neither cpufeatures nor libc. With protect, libc comes through secret-protection-core.
findings.impact: The platform dependency description is inaccurate. No missing license or runtime failure is established.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove LoongArch64 Linux from the cpufeatures clause while retaining the separate Unix protection dependency.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare the notice with cargo tree for LoongArch64 and AArch64, with and without protect.

remediation.evidence: Fresh LTO timing ratios are 1.00 in named GF(2^11) and Binary GF(2^10). Release and LTO assembly has no conditional jump on nonzero operand bits in any Field multiply/inverse arm; the documented zero-inverse distinction remains. Scoped to x86-64, Rust 1.99.1. Automation gap is AUD-007-BLD002.
Version, manifest, lockfiles and install guidance use 0.1.1. No v0.1.1 tag, attested package or publication was created or verified; the original artifact acceptance checks remain pending.

Compatible requirements and their rationale are recorded, secret-protection-core has minimum 0.1.1, lockfiles use zeroize 1.9.2 and landlock 0.4.8, and fresh strict tests pass.
The exact target commit still has 39 not yet committed entries. Pre-existing working-tree edits fill those entries, but they are not part of this commit. The original finding ID is retained.
The missing cfg-if notice and the general libc dependency outside protect are corrected. The narrower LoongArch64 error introduced in that text is tracked separately as AUD-007-DOC001.

Fresh alternating-holder timing is within a small factor of stable holders; 12-block stateful probes in both file fields pass with protected and allocator memory, including literal outcomes, fresh-search equivalence and step accounting. The 945-step known-answer test remains in the passing suite.

The Zeroize re-export has a caller-buffer wiping purpose documented without removing the compatible API.

limitations: Full review of the requested change range, not a new all-files baseline audit of unchanged repository code or every transitive dependency. Every one of the 55 changed files was assigned and reviewed; affected callers were followed beyond the diff.

Fresh execution is Linux x86-64 with Rust 1.99.1. No ARM/macOS/Windows runtime or assembly, Miri, forced allocation failure, statistical dudect campaign, or other compiler/optimization-level sweep was performed.

black_box is a best-effort compiler hint, not a language-level constant-time guarantee. The evidence establishes the inspected compiled configurations and the coarse regression probe; decoder error-dependent timing remains documented.
Retained proof/fuzz/fast-gate logs were hash-validated and their source diff reconstructed; they were not rerun. The historical runner lacks a separate post-command source fingerprint for every run.
The concurrent fix-coverage run had no completed JSON and command record when the report was prepared. No new line-coverage percentage is claimed; the existing 98.23% is explicitly historical.
No release was made, signed or published. v0.1.1 artifact bytes, attestation and crates.io checksum remain unverified. Only read-only remote queries were performed.
The original vulnerable whole checkout was not rebuilt. Existing baseline evidence was retained; no second working tree or project copy was created for this audit.
Independent reviewers were AI reviewers with separate scopes and a separate combined finding challenge; this is not an independent human security audit or proof of absence of defects.
informationalNotes: The current working tree contains pre-existing TECHNICAL.md/index edits and formatting corrections. They are not silently included in the committed verdict. Runtime builds used the two Rustfmt-normalized source files; exact normalized hashes are retained in snapshot.json.

The fresh holders measurement at 100,000 blocks gives 3.4 ns/step for two alternating holders versus 1.1 for stable holders; three alternating holders give 2.1 versus 0.9. These are diagnostic measurements, not a fixed performance guarantee. Fresh stateful assertions separately check correctness.

Timing: GF(2^11) median zero/random 2615/2609 ns, ratio 1.00; Binary GF(2^10) 3178/3176 ns, ratio 1.00. 41 interleaved rounds over 2048 words; acceptance uses median ratio 0.8 through 1.25. The observed Binary per-round maximum 1.28 is retained, not suppressed.

Assembly review covers Field::multiply and Field::inverse in both release library and LTO executable, including the gf256 inverse helper. Conditional branches select public field variants/degree or fixed loop bounds; the GF65536 inverse failure is the documented zero case. No operand-indexed memory table was found in those functions.

The supplied AUD-006 records have matching 15 finding IDs, all 32 procedure IDs and matching procedure hashes. All 23 extracted MHFE fixture lines match the pinned source vector; wordlist SHA-256 2f5eed53a4727b4bf8880d8f3f199efc90e58503646d9ff8eff3a2ed3b24dbda.

The library README convention calls for one documentation-index link and no contents table for a short README. AUD-006-DOC005 is withdrawn as an inconsistent requirement; the restored table and extra introduction links can be simplified in a later documentation change.
